**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/eu-frames-one-day-data-tools.html#/part-4-explore-declare-publish){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).

Part 4 turns the work of the day into a record that somebody else can find and rerun: a report rendered from the start, a history of its changes, and a place where it is deposited. One slide on the curve of alternative analyses of the claim shows why that record matters. The part takes ninety minutes.

## 1. The report as a record

**On the slides.** The slides show what `index.qmd` in the workspace holds, what rendering does, and what the render leaves behind.

To go further: [Quarto documents](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/quarto.html), on the AR4DS site.

## 2. Version control in practice

**On the shared screen.** The facilitator initialises a repository in the workspace, commits the report, reads a diff and commits again, and shows how the workspace publishes itself from GitHub. Nobody needs git today.

To go further: [Git and GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html), on the AR4DS site.

## 3. Hands-on 4 – The reproduction in a report

**In your workspace**, in the report `index.qmd`, or in your notes.

Fill the TODO of Task 3 with the analyst, the t and its degrees of freedom, and one sentence on how the model of your analyst differs from the other two. Add the check of Hands-on 3a as a chunk, and render the report. If you have git, commit and read a diff. If you work in the browser lab only, copy the cell of Task 3, its output and the check into your notes.

[Open the browser lab at Task 3](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

## 4. The curve of the claim

**On the slides.** The curve of 864 defensible analyses of the claim on one panel, with the five Multi100 results among them, shows what readable code makes possible once it exists.

To go further: [Multiverse](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd).

## 5. Repositories, archives and registries

**On the slides.** The slides cover the archives, statistical offices, repositories and registries in which finished work is kept, and the data of the case with the terms on which the data are held.

## 6. The SCORE dossier

[Open the SCORE dossier on the OSF](https://osf.io/h7432/){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

When the slides reach the dossier, open it and find the deposit of the analyst whom you reproduced.

To go further: [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd) and [Social science data sources](../../companion/data-sources.qmd).

## 7. The close

**On the slides.** The day closes on what you take with you, and the feedback form.

**By the end of the part** your reproduction sits in a rendered report or in your notes, with the check that would have caught the slip of your analyst, and you know where a finished analysis is deposited and on what terms.
